title: Black War in Tasmania
summary: Violent frontier conflict between Tasmanian Aboriginal people and British settlers and authorities in Van Diemen's Land, dated from about 1824 by the National Museum of Australia. Lieutenant-Governor George Arthur declared martial law on 1 November 1828, and in October–November 1830 the 'Black Line' sweep failed to capture many Aboriginal people; later efforts removed them to Flinders Island.

uncertainty.note: NMA dates the war's start to 'about 1824'; other scholarship dates it differently. End set at the Black Line (1830); removals to Flinders Island followed.

where.modern_name: Tasmania, Australia (pin at Hobart, a proxy for the island-wide conflict)

importance.justification: Described by NMA as the most extensive conflict in Australian history; it devastated Tasmanian Aboriginal communities.

audience_note: Describes colonial violence against Aboriginal people, including killings of women and children.
reviewer_note: Start date varies by source (NMA 'about 1824'; Britannica snippet says 1804, not opened). Pin is Hobart as a proxy. NMA's 'fewer than 2,000 by about 1818' looked odd, so no population figures used.
